learningObjectives.title: Hindu beliefs about God and Brahman

questions.q: In Hindu belief, what does the term 'Brahman' refer to?
options: The ultimate reality and universal spirit underlying everything
The priestly class within Hindu society
A sacred river in northern India
The cycle of birth, death and rebirth
questions.explain: Brahman is the one supreme, eternal reality from which all things come.

questions.q: The Trimurti consists of Brahma, Vishnu and which other deity?
questions.explain: The Trimurti expresses Brahman as Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver and Shiva the destroyer.

questions.q: Within the Trimurti, Vishnu is best known as the...?
questions.explain: Vishnu is the preserver who maintains and protects the universe.

questions.q: In Hinduism, the 'atman' refers to...?
options: The eternal soul or self within a living being
questions.explain: The atman is the eternal soul, believed to be part of Brahman.

questions.q: Brahman described as being beyond all form and human qualities is known as...?
questions.explain: Nirguna means 'without qualities', describing Brahman as beyond human form and understanding.

questions.q: When Brahman is understood as having form and qualities, for example in the deities, this is called...?
questions.explain: Saguna means 'with qualities', Brahman experienced in a personal form such as a deity.

questions.q: Rama and Krishna are traditionally understood by Hindus to be...?
questions.explain: An avatar is a descent of Vishnu to earth, and Rama and Krishna are two of his most important avatars.

questions.q: The general Hindu term for worship is...?
questions.explain: Puja is worship, which may take place in the home or at the mandir (temple).

questions.q: During worship, the ritual of offering light by moving a lit lamp before the deity is called...?
questions.explain: In arti, a lamp with lit wicks (divas) is moved in front of the murti as an offering of light.

questions.q: Hindus regard the River Ganges as especially sacred and bathe in it at the pilgrimage city of...?
questions.explain: Varanasi on the banks of the Ganges is one of the holiest Hindu pilgrimage sites.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a murti in Hindu worship?
options: It provides a physical focus that helps the worshipper concentrate on the deity
It is believed to be a river god
It records the stages of life
It is the blessed food shared after worship
questions.explain: A murti is an image or statue that acts as a focus and aid for worshipping the deity.

questions.q: In the context of worship, 'darshan' means...?
options: Seeing and being seen by the deity
questions.explain: Darshan is the auspicious experience of viewing the murti and being seen by the deity.

questions.q: A Hindu travels to Varanasi and bathes in the Ganges. What do they most commonly hope this act will achieve?
options: The washing away of sins and bad karma
Immediate promotion to a higher varna
The end of the festival of Holi
The creation of a new murti
questions.explain: Bathing in the sacred Ganges is believed to cleanse a person of sins and bad karma.

questions.q: Diwali is commonly known as the festival of...?
questions.explain: Diwali is the festival of lights, marked by the lighting of many divas (lamps).

questions.q: Which deity is especially worshipped during Diwali, being associated with wealth and good fortune?
questions.explain: Lakshmi, goddess of wealth and prosperity, is welcomed into homes during Diwali.

questions.q: The festival of Holi is linked to the story of Prahlad and Holika because it celebrates...?
options: The triumph of good over evil
The duty of the warrior class
questions.explain: Holi recalls how the devout Prahlad was saved while the demoness Holika perished, symbolising good overcoming evil.

questions.q: The term 'varnashramadharma' refers to a Hindu's duties according to their...?
questions.explain: Varnashramadharma is the duty appropriate to one's varna (social class) and ashrama (stage of life).

questions.q: A Hindu family cleans their home, lights rows of divas and welcomes Lakshmi with prayers for prosperity. Which festival are they most likely celebrating?
questions.explain: Lighting divas and welcoming Lakshmi for good fortune are central features of Diwali.

questions.q: A young Hindu is focused on studying religious texts and remaining celibate under a teacher. Which ashrama (stage of life) are they in?
questions.explain: Brahmacharya is the student stage, devoted to learning and self-discipline.

questions.q: A Hindu believes that carrying out their responsibilities honestly and caring for their family is a religious obligation. This sense of religious and moral duty is known as...?
questions.explain: Dharma is the religious and moral duty each Hindu is expected to fulfil.
